topic: things astronauts genuinely can't do in space -- crying, burping, whistling, and height change
title: Things Astronauts Genuinely Can't Do In Space
description: AI-narrated commentary. Crying, burping, whistling, even your own height -- space changes things you'd never expect. NASA-documented surprises about everyday life in zero gravity.

hook_candidates.text: Things astronauts genuinely can't do once they're in space.
Astronauts can't cry properly, burp normally, or whistle outside their suit.
What's something completely normal on Earth that's impossible in space?
You'd think crying, burping, and whistling would work the same in space -- they don't.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who always says space life must be basically the same as ours, because they want to prove it very much isn't.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume astronauts can still cry, burp, and whistle normally once they're in space.

sources.note: Confirms zero-g prevents gas separating from liquid, so a burp brings both up instead.
Confirms astronauts temporarily gain about 2 inches in height from spinal disc expansion.

beats.text: Things astronauts genuinely **can't** do once they're in space.
Crying in space doesn't work like you'd **expect**.
Tears just **pool** up and sting your eyes instead.
Worse than not crying at all, honestly.
Gas can't separate from liquid, so a burp brings **both** up.
Nobody mentions that part in training.
Suits don't hold enough air pressure to whistle -- but the station **does**.
Bad suit design, not a space mystery.
The strangest one: astronauts actually grow **taller** in space.
Without gravity compressing the spine, discs expand -- adding about **two inches**.
Researchers still don't know the **long-term** effects.
So it turns out there are some...
